page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8 is an x86_64 instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 8 execution threads, running on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, backed by support for instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance delivers 62.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance type does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core efficiency, with the instance scoring 2270.0 in Geekbench single-core and 3059.0 in text processing, placing both in the top tier of evaluated systems. Compression and decompression tests show strength, reaching 34.83 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.96 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded metrics fall in the middle tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 8519.0, a PassMark CPU score of 12270.59, and a Redis SET throughput of 12.37 million operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 61.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 35.37 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost efficiency and architectural perspective, the 1:7.75 core-to-memory ratio provides significant memory capacity without forcing the provisioning of unnecessary compute cores. Without integrated local storage, the instance relies on remote block storage for persistent data, which introduces external I/O considerations. The platform is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise software, in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and web application runtimes.
